intents: Expose the internal HTTP service through a public floating VIP using DNAT on the frontier node edge2.
The final state must have VIP 203.0.113.100/32 active on edge2 eth1.
Map TCP 203.0.113.100:8080 to the internal server 10.0.2.100:8080.
Add forward rules that allow the DNAT flow and its return traffic.
Use SNAT/MASQUERADE so return traffic is symmetric and does not depend on changing the server application.
Do not flush/reset iptables and do not modify existing addressing or management connectivity.

srv: ip route add default via 10.0.2.1 metric 1024

edge2: iptables -A FORWARD -p tcp -d 10.0.2.100 --dport 8080 -m conntrack --ctstate NEW,ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A FORWARD -p tcp -s 10.0.2.100 --sport 8080 -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT

ground_truth_reasoning: The failover target is edge2, so the VIP belongs on edge2 eth1 in the final state. PREROUTING DNAT maps client connections for 203.0.113.100:8080 to the internal server at 10.0.2.100:8080. Forward rules permit both the new inbound flow and the established return direction. POSTROUTING MASQUERADE toward the internal server makes return traffic symmetric through edge2, while preserving all existing management and base addressing.
